alt: Two tiffin boxes taped together carry the same weight as before, while two meals poured into one box are lighter to carry but mix a little.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves on an office pantry counter in an Indian workplace, with a microwave and a water dispenser in the background. LEFT panel: a young office worker in his late 20s, formal shirt and lanyard, holds two round steel tiffin carriers taped together with thick brown packing tape around their middles; he strains slightly as he lifts them, a little weight icon above showing the same heavy load as before. The two separate meals are visible through a cutaway, rajma rice in one and chole roti in the other, untouched. RIGHT panel: a colleague, a woman in her late 20s with a kurta and a lanyard, pours both meals into one larger tiffin, the rajma and chole touching and swirling a little at the border, and lifts it easily with one hand, a lighter weight icon floating above it; a tiny swirl icon marks where the flavours mix. Bright pantry tube lights and a cheerful lunch-break mood. Labels: "CONCATENATE" at the top of the left panel, "SUM" at the top of the right panel.

key: Before a long road trip, you test the
name: ch07_road_trip_test_cheap_first
alt: A family tests a car around their colony, then on a short highway run, then takes the best car on the full trip and compares mileage.
scene: A long horizontal road scene in four stages from left to right, like a journey strip. STAGE 1: inside a quiet residential colony with gates, neem trees and a watchman, a young man in his 30s in a T-shirt drives a small old hatchback slowly round the block, checking the dashboard, a spanner icon floating above for testing the setup. STAGE 2: on a short stretch of highway with a toll plaza, he drives a mid-size sedan, a small checklist bubble with ticks above it. STAGE 3: on a long scenic highway through hills toward a distant mountain range, the whole family, wife, two kids and grandmother, travel in a large comfortable SUV loaded with luggage on the roof, happy and relaxed. STAGE 4: at a roadside dhaba at sunset, the man compares three small cards pinned on a board, one per car, each showing a fuel pump icon and a rupee sign, and a line chart connecting them like a curve. A thin road line runs along the bottom connecting all four stages. Warm daylight shifting to sunset from left to right. Labels: "CHEAP TEST" above stage 1, "FULL RUN" above stage 3, and "COMPARE" above stage 4.

key: Learning to drive in a ghat road
name: ch07_ghat_road_hyperparameters
alt: A learner drives on a winding mountain road, zigzagging when turning too hard and drifting when too gentle, while an instructor grades the driving.
scene: A winding ghat road climbing a green hillside in the Western Ghats during monsoon, with mist, waterfalls, hairpin bends and stone parapets, seen from above. A white learner car with an L sign drives up the road, its path drawn three ways in coloured lines along one bend: a red zigzag swerving left and right too sharply, a blue line drifting wide off the curve towards the edge, and a smooth green line hugging the bend perfectly. Along the roadside, a series of small road signs is grouped in sets with a bracket, showing how many signs are read before each correction. A small inset in the corner shows the same car on a loop of the same route, a lap counter reading many laps, with the driver mechanically mouthing directions with glazed eyes. Inside the car, a learner in her early 20s grips the wheel nervously, while a driving instructor in his 50s with a thick moustache and a checked shirt holds a scorecard, marking how she drives and ignoring her repeated recitation of the directions. Moody monsoon light, wet glossy road. Labels: "LEARNING RATE" beside the coloured paths, "BATCH SIZE" beside the grouped signs, "EPOCHS" beside the lap counter inset.

key: hire a better coach and new bowling
name: ch08_cricket_academy_data_centric
alt: A cricket academy either hires a star coach with new bowling machines, or keeps its coach and gives players better nets, match footage and real spin practice.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves at the same cricket academy ground in an Indian city with green nets, a small pavilion and a scoreboard. LEFT panel: a flashy new head coach in sunglasses and a designer tracksuit arrives with assistants wheeling in three shiny new bowling machines still wrapped in plastic; a banner of a price tag flutters above. The young players stand in a line watching, not yet practising. RIGHT panel: the same old coach, a grey-haired man in his 60s with a faded academy cap and a whistle, runs a smart session: players in whites bat in nets against a real leg-spinner bowling sharp turn; a laptop on a plastic table plays match footage of real opponents, and a whiteboard shows a field map of where the balls actually go in matches; a stack of labelled practice balls sits ready. The players are sweaty, focused and improving, a rising arrow behind them. Bright late-afternoon sunlight, long shadows across the turf. Labels: "MODEL-CENTRIC" at the top of the left panel, "DATA-CENTRIC" at the top of the right panel.

key: checking stock in the back room
name: ch08_kirana_assistant_full_sequence
alt: A shop owner teaches a new assistant the full sequence of serving a customer: checking the back room, showing the payment QR code and saying one minute.
scene: A cosy neighbourhood kirana shop seen from the customer side, shelves packed with biscuit packets, oil tins, rice sacks and soap bars, a glass counter in front with a small weighing scale. A numbered sequence of four steps runs left to right along the counter like a comic strip, all featuring the same new assistant, a shy boy of about 18 in a striped T-shirt, guided by the owner, a man in his 50s in a white vest and lungi with a pencil behind his ear. STEP 1: a customer, a young mother with a toddler, asks for something; the assistant listens. STEP 2: the assistant turns and says "one minute" in a small speech bubble. STEP 3: he walks through a curtain into a dim back room stacked with cartons, checking a shelf with a torch. STEP 4: he returns with the item and holds up a payment QR code standee while the customer scans it with her phone. Above the strip, the owner points at a notebook where each step is written as a little icon, emphasising that every side step must be shown, not only the final hand-over. Warm evening shop light, a tube light flickering. Labels: "WHOLE SEQUENCE" above the strip, "SIDE STEPS" pointing at steps 2 and 3.

key: Multi-turn data is like the IRCTC
name: ch08_railway_counter_multi_turn
alt: A railway booking clerk and a passenger go back and forth over date, quota and class, compared with a single question answered in one line.
scene: A railway reservation counter in a busy Indian station hall, with a grille window, a printed timetable on the wall and a queue behind. The scene is split by a thin vertical line. LEFT, larger panel: a passenger in his 40s in a checked shirt with a cloth bag leans to the window; between him and the clerk, a woman in her 30s with spectacles, a cardigan and a computer, a vertical chain of five alternating speech bubbles zigzags downward like a conversation: a small calendar icon with a question mark; a bubble with two options, a lightning bolt and a plain ticket; a bubble from the clerk with a crossed-out seat and a different seat offered; a nod from the passenger; and finally a printed ticket sliding out. RIGHT, narrower panel: the same clerk answers a single quick question from a student about whether a train goes to a city, one bubble and one reply, then the student leaves. Fluorescent light, ceiling fans, a big clock and a busy, practical mood. Labels: "MULTI-TURN" at the top of the left panel, "SINGLE-TURN" at the top of the right panel.

key: Six checks a good chai stall owner does
name: ch08_chai_stall_milk_checks
alt: A chai stall owner inspects milk packets in six ways: is it milk, full cream, same every day, not leaking, not billed twice, and from a licensed dairy.
scene: A roadside chai stall at dawn, a kettle on a stove, glass tumblers and biscuit jars. In the centre, the chai stall owner, a woman in her 40s in a cotton saree with the pallu tied at her waist, sits on a stool with a crate of milk packets and inspects them carefully. Around her, six small numbered inset bubbles form a ring, each showing one check with a simple drawing: a packet held up with a milk-drop icon and a tick; a creamy thick drop next to a thin watery one; two identical packets from different days side by side with an equal sign; a leaking packet dripping onto the ground, set aside; a bill with the same line written twice and one struck out; a dairy certificate with a stamp and a small seal. A delivery boy on a bicycle with a crate of packets waits at the side. Behind, the street wakes up: a milkman's van, a newspaper boy, pigeons, and two early customers in woollen caps wait for their first cup. Soft golden dawn light, steam from the kettle. Labels: "DATA QUALITY" arching above the ring of checks, "REJECT" beside the leaking packet.

key: perfect dal alone (quality, no variety)
name: ch08_thali_quality_and_variety
alt: Three thalis: one bowl of perfect dal, ten sloppy dishes, and ten well-made dishes, with two regional thalis showing different proportions.
scene: A long dining table seen from above in an Indian restaurant, with three steel thali plates in a row, and a smaller row of two plates below. TOP LEFT thali: just one bowl of beautifully made dal with a ghee swirl in an otherwise empty plate; a diner's hand hovers above it with a slightly disappointed shrug. TOP MIDDLE thali: ten bowls filled with sloppy, spilled, oddly coloured dishes, burnt rotis and runny curd; a small frown icon. TOP RIGHT thali: ten neat bowls of well-made dishes, glossy sabzi, fluffy rice, crisp papad, fresh salad, a sweet; a big smile icon and a gold star. BOTTOM ROW: two more complete thalis side by side, each with different proportions of dishes: one with many sweet dishes and dhokla, one with fish curry, rice and mustard greens, served to two different diners, an older man in a white cotton boat-shaped cap and a woman in a red-bordered white saree, each smiling at their own plate. Warm overhead light, brass and steel gleaming. Labels: "QUALITY" over the top-left plate, "VARIETY" over the top-middle plate, and "BOTH" over the top-right plate.

key: Learning to drive in Bengaluru traffic
name: ch08_driving_lessons_diminishing_returns
alt: A learner's driving improves quickly at first and then slowly, while a scooter rider who already knows the road needs fewer lessons.
scene: A busy Indian city street at a traffic junction with autos, buses, two-wheelers, a traffic policeman on a podium and a flyover overhead, seen from a slightly raised angle. Across the top of the frame, a curving path of milestone signboards rises steeply at first and then flattens, each signboard marked with an hours count. Along the path, the same learner, a young woman in her mid 20s in a salwar kameez with a dupatta tied back, sits in a white learner car with a big L sign: at the first milestone she looks terrified and stalls the car; at the second she is driving carefully but confidently; at the far flat end she makes a small perfect lane change with a relaxed smile. Below, in the foreground, a second learner, a young man in a denim jacket who already rides a scooter, parked beside him, steps into a learner car and drives off smoothly, overtaking the first learner's early position with a shorter path drawn on the ground. A driving school instructor in a cap stands at the corner with a clipboard. Hazy evening light, warm and humorous mood. Labels: "BIG GAINS" near the steep start of the path, "SMALL GAINS" near the flat end, "STRONG BASE" beside the scooter rider.

key: A data flywheel is like a popular
name: ch08_restaurant_data_flywheel
alt: A popular restaurant's orders produce ratings, ratings tell the kitchen what to fix, better dishes bring more orders, in a turning wheel.
scene: A circular composition built around a big wooden flywheel standing upright in the centre of a busy cloud kitchen in an Indian city. Around the rim of the wheel, four scenes are placed at the four points of the circle, connected by thick curved arrows going clockwise. TOP: delivery riders on scooters carry insulated bags out of the kitchen door, a stack of order slips flying. RIGHT: a phone screen inset shows rows of star ratings and small comments, and a reorder button glowing. BOTTOM: a head chef in her 30s with a white cap and a notebook reads a printout of ratings and circles one dish, then corrects a sabzi recipe with two cooks. LEFT: more customers, a family, a student, an office worker, tap order buttons on their phones, little hearts above them. The wheel spins faster with motion lines. On the far right edge, outside the circle, a rival restaurant owner in a blazer stands with a briefcase of cash, but the wheel's ratings are locked behind a glass wall he cannot reach. Bright kitchen light, energetic mood. Labels: "DATA FLYWHEEL" across the hub of the wheel, "MOAT" on the glass wall.

key: Board exam paper checkers get a marking
name: ch08_marking_scheme_guidelines
alt: Two teachers give different marks to the same answer, and with a marking scheme sheet they agree.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a board exam evaluation centre: a classroom with long tables, bundles of answer sheets tied with string, a ceiling fan and a peon carrying chai. In both halves, two teachers sit side by side checking photocopies of the same student answer. LEFT panel: a teacher in her 50s with a cotton saree and spectacles writes a big "4" in red ink on her copy; beside her a teacher in his 40s with a sweater vest writes a big "2" on his copy; they glance at each other with raised eyebrows, a jagged crack symbol between their scores. RIGHT panel: the same two teachers now have a printed marking-scheme sheet pinned between them, with three short lines shown as icons: a formula symbol with two check marks, a unit symbol with one check mark, a final answer box; they both write the same score and nod, and a matching green equal sign floats between their papers. Bright tube-light glow, stacks of paper everywhere, focused mood. Labels: "NO GUIDELINE" at the top of the left panel, "GUIDELINE" at the top of the right panel.

key: Augmentation is photocopying your real
name: ch08_id_card_augment_vs_synthesis
alt: A tester photocopies a real ID card at different angles for a scanner test, while a designer creates sample ID cards with made-up names in the same layout.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, set in a small software testing lab in an Indian office with a document scanner on each desk. LEFT panel: a young tester in his mid 20s with a hoodie and an office lanyard places one real ID card on a photocopier glass at different tilts and angles; a fan of photocopies spreads out on the desk, each showing the same card rotated, darker, lighter or slightly blurred, with every detail on the card drawn only as grey bars and a face square so no number is legible. RIGHT panel: a designer in her late 20s with short hair and big headphones sits at a monitor creating new sample ID cards in the exact same layout, each with a different cartoon face and placeholder grey text bars, a printer spitting out a stack of them; a sticky note on the monitor reads "SAMPLE" in bold. Both stacks feed into a document scanner in the background that lights up green. Cool office light, focused testing mood. Labels: "AUGMENTATION" at the top of the left panel, "SYNTHESIS" at the top of the right panel.

key: the teacher keeps the same question
name: ch08_mock_exam_question_template
alt: A teacher fills the blanks of one train question template with different numbers to produce a stack of practice papers.
scene: A coaching-class staff room in an Indian town: a cluttered wooden table, a stack of old question papers, a calculator, a steel tumbler of tea and a wall calendar with exam dates circled. A maths teacher in his 50s with a grey moustache, half-sleeve shirt and a pen tucked in the pocket sits with a single template card in front of him; the card shows a simple sketch of a train leaving a station with two empty blank boxes where the speed and distance go. Beside him, a small machine-like hand-cranked press, drawn playfully, takes the template and number tiles from a bowl and stamps out practice papers one after another, each with the same train sketch but different numbers in the boxes; the papers pile up into a tall stack of a hundred. On the right, in a small inset, a student in a school uniform faces a totally different question, a sketch of a water tank with pipes, and scratches his head with a question mark. Warm afternoon light through a barred window. Labels: "TEMPLATE" on the card, "RULE-BASED" above the stamping press, "NEW TYPE" above the student inset.

key: NDRF teams rehearse building collapses
name: ch08_rescue_drill_simulation
alt: A disaster rescue team rehearses at a mock collapsed building site, while an inset shows the messier real scene with crowds and monsoon mud.
scene: A wide outdoor training ground with a purpose-built mock collapsed building made of concrete slabs, broken walls and twisted rods, under a clear sky. A disaster rescue team in orange uniforms, helmets with headlamps and boots works methodically: two members crawl into a gap with a stretcher, one uses a hydraulic cutter on a slab, another lowers a dog on a harness, and a team leader in her 30s with a radio and clipboard times the drill with a stopwatch. A dummy victim in a red jacket is carried out on a stretcher. Neat cones and tape mark the drill area. In the top right corner, a smaller inset framed like a photo shows a real scene after an earthquake in pouring monsoon rain: thick brown mud, a panicked crowd held back by police, umbrellas, and tangled electric wires, much messier than the drill. A thin gap line separates the inset from the main scene. Clear bright daylight on the drill, dark stormy light in the inset. Labels: "SIMULATION" over the main drill ground, "REAL WORLD" over the inset, "SIM2REAL GAP" on the dividing line.

key: Back-translation is how a careful
name: ch08_back_translation_check
alt: One translator turns an English notice into Hindi, a second translator who never saw the English turns it back, and the two English versions are compared.
scene: A three-step left-to-right composition in a small translation bureau in an Indian city, desks with stacks of legal documents, a fan and a shelf of dictionaries. LEFT: a translator in her 40s in a cotton saree and spectacles writes a Hindi version of an English legal notice; the English page has neat grey lines, and her Hindi page has Devanagari-style squiggles drawn as abstract lines. MIDDLE: separated by a closed door with a small "no peeking" sign showing a crossed-out eye, a second translator, a young man in a kurta with a laptop, receives only the Hindi page and writes it back into English. RIGHT: the first translator holds the two English pages up side by side to a window; most lines match with green ticks, but one line is highlighted in red with a mismatch symbol, and she circles it on the Hindi page with a red pen. Dotted arrows connect the three steps in a loop from English to Hindi to English. Soft daylight, careful, scholarly mood. Labels: "TRANSLATE" over the left step, "BACK" over the middle step, "COMPARE" over the right step.

key: Reverse instruction is like a quiz
name: ch08_quiz_master_reverse_instruction
alt: A quiz master reads a good encyclopedia article and writes the question whose answer is that article.
scene: A school auditorium preparing for an inter-school quiz, with a stage, a big buzzer board, and banners in the background. In the foreground, a quiz master in his 40s, round spectacles, a bandhgala jacket and a neat beard, sits at a desk under a lamp. In his left hand is a long, well-written encyclopedia article printed on several pages with a star of quality stamped at the top. With his right hand he writes a short question on a small index card. A thick arrow is drawn backward, from the finished article to the question card, emphasising the reverse direction. On the right, a smaller faded inset shows the usual way: a nervous student at a desk sweating as he tries to write a long article in answer to a question card, with crossings-out and blots and a crumpled pile of failed drafts at his feet. In the background on stage, a quiz contestant team of three students in blazers waits with their buzzer. Warm lamp light in a dim auditorium, studious mood. Labels: "ANSWER FIRST" over the article, "QUESTION" over the index card.

key: A sweet shop that makes laddoos by
name: ch08_laddoo_machine_quality_check
alt: A quality checker at a sweet factory weighs machine-made laddoos, tastes a sample, and sends a batch to a lab.
scene: A small sweet factory floor in an Indian town, bright and clean, with a stainless steel machine on the left pushing out a steady line of round orange laddoos onto a conveyor belt. Along the belt, three checks happen from left to right, all by the same quality checker, a woman in her 40s in a white coat, hair net and gloves. CHECK 1: she places laddoos one by one on a small digital weighing scale; a rejected misshapen one is tossed into a reject tray. CHECK 2: she bites into a sample laddoo with a thoughtful expression, a small tasting card in her hand with a star rating. CHECK 3: she seals a small box of laddoos into a padded envelope addressed to a lab, where a small inset shows a lab technician in goggles testing it with test tubes. At the end of the belt, neatly packed boxes stack up on a trolley with a green tick. In the background, a shop window shows customers waiting. Bright fluorescent factory light, clean and cheerful mood. Labels: "HEURISTIC" over the weighing scale, "AI JUDGE" over the tasting step, "FUNCTIONAL" over the lab envelope.

key: copies his dishes until a small cloud
name: ch08_chef_apprentice_distillation
alt: A senior chef's apprentice copies his dishes in a small cloud kitchen at a fraction of the cost, and in an inset a later apprentice surpasses the master.
scene: A split composition with a large main scene and a smaller inset. MAIN SCENE, divided by a dotted arrow from left to right: on the left, a grand restaurant kitchen with copper pots and a big brigade, where a famous senior chef in his 60s with a tall white hat and a white moustache plates an elaborate biryani; a young apprentice in his early 20s in a plain apron watches closely and copies each step in a small notebook. On the right, the same apprentice now runs a tiny cloud kitchen with one gas stove and a single helper, packing nearly identical biryani boxes for delivery riders, a small rupee coin icon above showing low cost and the price sticker on each box much lower. INSET in the top right corner: years later, a different apprentice, a woman in her 30s, stands in a large modern kitchen of her own with a trophy on the shelf, while the old master tastes her dish with surprised raised eyebrows. A small padlocked recipe book sits on a shelf in the master's kitchen, hinting at trade secrets. Warm kitchen light and steam. Labels: "TEACHER" above the senior chef, "STUDENT" above the apprentice in the cloud kitchen.

key: first remove duplicate entries (fast)
name: ch08_wedding_rsvp_dedup_first
alt: A wedding organiser first crosses out duplicate names on a copy of the RSVP list, then calls the remaining guests, keeping the original list safe.
scene: A home office corner in an Indian house during wedding preparations, with sweet boxes stacked in a corner, a garland on the doorframe and a wall calendar with the wedding date circled. On the desk lies the original RSVP list in a plastic sleeve, sealed with a small padlock sticker, untouched. Beside it, the organiser, the bride's brother in his late 20s in a T-shirt and track pants, works on a photocopied version of the list in two steps shown left to right. STEP 1: with a quick highlighter, he crosses out repeated names that appear twice, connected by little curved lines; a small lightning icon shows this is fast. STEP 2: with a phone to his ear and the shorter list in front of him, he ticks off each guest as he calls them, a small hourglass icon showing this is slow; a few ticks are green, a few have little question marks. In a faded side inset, a version of him making phone calls first, calling the same aunty twice and getting scolded. Warm evening lamp light, busy festive atmosphere. Labels: "DEDUP" over step 1, "VERIFY" over step 2, "ORIGINAL" on the sealed list.

key: A new kitchen manager tastes every dish
name: ch08_kitchen_manager_tastes_data
alt: A new kitchen manager tastes each dish on her first day while sales reports sit on the counter, catching one curry that is far too salty.
scene: A restaurant kitchen in an Indian city on a weekday morning, seen at counter height. A long steel pass counter runs across the frame with a row of a dozen small bowls of different dishes: dal, two sabzis, paneer, a chicken curry, raita, rice. The new kitchen manager, a woman in her 30s in a black chef coat with her hair tied back and a tasting spoon in hand, moves along the row tasting each one; most get a small green tick card placed in front. At one bowl of curry she grimaces, eyes squeezed shut, a salt shaker icon bursting above her head. Behind that bowl, a young cook in a white cap with a heavy hand on the salt container looks sheepish. On the left end of the counter lie a stack of sales printouts and a laptop with bar charts, slightly pushed aside, useful but not showing the salt problem. In the background, other cooks prepare vegetables and a big exhaust hood hums. Bright morning light, a sense of discovery. Labels: "LOOK AT DATA" above the manager, "REPORTS" over the printouts.

key: A voter list with the same person
name: ch08_voter_list_fuzzy_duplicates
alt: An election officer finds the same person entered three times in a voter list with slightly different spellings, using a magnifying glass to link them.
scene: A polling booth set up in a government school classroom in an Indian town, with a wooden desk, a ballot box sealed with string, a banner with a voting finger symbol and indelible ink bottle. In the centre, an election officer in her 40s with a cotton saree and a lanyard leans over a big printed voter register. Three rows on the page are highlighted: two that look identical, joined by a short straight line marked with an equals sign, and a third shortened name with an initial, joined to the others by a longer wavy dotted line through a magnifying glass she holds. Next to the desk, the same man stands in a queue three times as three ghostly copies of himself, a middle-aged man in a white kurta and white cotton boat-shaped cap, each holding up an inked finger, with a playful three-times symbol above. In a small inset at the corner, two genuinely different men with the same name stand side by side, one tall and one short, with a caution sign. Bright daylight through classroom windows, civic mood. Labels: "EXACT MATCH" on the straight line, "FUZZY MATCH" on the wavy line.

key: the clerk is trained on the official
name: ch08_reservation_form_template_mismatch
alt: A railway clerk processes a standard reservation form quickly, but slows down and makes mistakes on the same details written on a plain sheet with extra text.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, at the same railway reservation window with a steel grille, a computer and a rubber stamp. The clerk in both halves is a man in his 50s with a grey moustache, round spectacles and a pale blue uniform shirt. LEFT panel: a passenger hands him the official printed form with neat boxes in the usual layout; he types smoothly, a fast motion line and a green tick on the screen. RIGHT panel: another passenger hands him a plain ruled sheet with the same details scribbled in a different order, starting with a flowery greeting line "Dear Sir" at the top; the clerk squints and frowns, sweat appearing on his forehead, typing a wrong detail as a red cross appears on his screen, a small hourglass beside him. A small poster on the wall behind the clerk shows the official form layout, as if he trained on it. A long queue, a big station clock and a ceiling fan fill the background. Neutral station light. Labels: "TRAINING FORMAT" at the top of the left panel, "MISMATCH" at the top of the right panel.

key: A chai stall with the best recipe in
name: ch09_chai_stall_speed_and_cost
alt: A chai stall with a prized recipe loses its office crowd to the next stall because each cup takes too long and costs too much to make.
scene: A street corner outside a glass office tower in an Indian city at nine in the morning. On the left, a proud chai stall with a framed handwritten recipe card hanging on the post and a small trophy on the shelf; its owner, a man in his 50s with a white moustache and a woolen cap, slowly stirs a single cup with great care, a large clock icon above him showing twenty minutes and a big rupee coin icon stacked high showing an expensive cup. A long queue of office workers in shirts, kurtas and lanyards, checking their watches, slowly peels away from his stall. Dotted footprints lead them to the right, to a plain neighbouring stall where a young chaiwala in a vest pours a long stream of tea into a row of glasses at once, cheap and quick, with a small coin and a short stopwatch above. The proud owner holds up his recipe card in protest while the crowd sips happily next door. Morning sunlight reflecting off the tower's glass, steam rising, a busy commuter mood. Labels: "QUALITY" over the framed recipe card, "SPEED AND COST" above the busy neighbouring stall.

key: Training is a cricket academy spending
name: ch09_academy_fee_vs_match_fees
alt: A cricket academy trains a batter for years for a one-time fee, and afterwards he earns match fees across many matches that pay it back.
scene: A left-to-right timeline composition. LEFT third: a cricket academy net session spread over several seasons, shown as three small stacked vignettes of the same batter growing from a skinny 12-year-old to a strong 18-year-old in whites, practising with a coach; a single large one-time bill with a rupee sign is pinned to the academy gate, labelled with a heavy weight icon. RIGHT two-thirds: a long row of small stadium icons stretching into the distance, each a match the grown batter plays, with floodlights, crowds and a scoreboard; above each stadium hangs a small coin, and the coins drop into a big jar at the bottom right that steadily fills; a line of dotted arrows shows the jar level rising until it overtakes the height of the original academy bill. The batter, now in a coloured team jersey with a helmet under his arm, waves to fans in the nearest stadium. Bright afternoon light on the academy, evening floodlights over the stadiums. Labels: "TRAINING" over the academy section, "INFERENCE" over the row of stadiums, "PAYBACK" beside the coin jar.

key: The counter clerk and queue system
name: ch09_reservation_service_vs_server
alt: At a railway reservation office, clerks and a token system take and check forms, then send them to a back-room booking engine on big computers that allots seats.
scene: A cutaway view of a railway reservation building, front hall on the left and a back machine room on the right, separated by a wall with a pneumatic tube running through it. LEFT, the front hall: a token-number display board, rows of steel chairs with waiting passengers holding forms, and three windows where clerks in pale blue uniforms check forms, stamp them and slip each into a capsule that goes into the tube; a supervisor in a grey sweater directs which tube each form goes into, for different trains. RIGHT, the back room: a booking engine drawn as a large tall cabinet with a seat chart screen of coach diagrams, connected by thick cables to racks of humming computers with blinking lights; an engineer in a checked shirt and lanyard monitors it. Capsules arrive from the tube, and on the seat chart one berth lights up green as a seat is allotted. A long thin thread shows the computers still busy writing out a long ticket printout for one request. Fluorescent light in the hall, cool blue light in the machine room. Labels: "SERVICE" over the front hall, "SERVER" over the booking engine, "HARDWARE" over the computer racks.

key: A kirana shop at Diwali. If the
name: ch09_diwali_shop_compute_vs_bandwidth
alt: At a Diwali rush, one shop is slowed by slow billing and adds cashiers, while another bills instantly but waits on a stock boy fetching every item from a distant godown.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a kirana shop decorated for Diwali with strings of lights, paper lanterns and boxes of sweets and dry fruit, a crowd of festive customers at the counter. LEFT panel: the shopkeeper, an older man in a white kurta, fumbles slowly with a calculator and a long handwritten bill while a queue piles up; to fix it, two more cashiers with calculators squeeze in beside him and the queue shrinks, a green arrow shows speed rising. RIGHT panel: the billing machine is instant, but a stock boy of about 16 in a sweaty T-shirt runs with a single item at a time from the shop to a godown down the road and back, a long dotted path with footprints; behind the counter, three extra cashiers stand idle with arms folded and nothing to bill, while customers wait. A small inset shows a faster tempo van on a wider road between shop and godown as the real fix. Warm festive lights, crowded cheerful chaos. Labels: "COMPUTE-BOUND" at the top of the left panel, "BANDWIDTH-BOUND" at the top of the right panel.

key: Moving house with a small auto-rickshaw
name: ch09_auto_rickshaw_sofa_capacity
alt: A sofa does not fit in a small auto-rickshaw, so it is taken apart and moved in many trips, making the speed of trips the real limit.
scene: A residential lane outside a small Indian apartment building on moving day, cardboard boxes stacked on the footpath. Composed left to right in three moments. LEFT: two movers in vests and towels on their heads try to push a big three-seater sofa into a small three-wheeler goods auto; it sticks out comically, a red cross above it, and the driver shakes his head. MIDDLE: the movers take the sofa apart with screwdrivers, into cushions, arms, the base and the backrest, arranged neatly on the ground. RIGHT: the same auto makes many trips along a looping dotted road to a new building down the street, each trip carrying one sofa piece; a counter in a bubble shows trip numbers going up, and a stopwatch icon floats above the road, showing that how fast each trip goes now decides the moving time. The homeowner, a young woman in a T-shirt and jeans with a clipboard, watches the clock anxiously. Bright morning light, dust in the air, comic mood. Labels: "CAPACITY" above the stuck sofa, "BANDWIDTH" above the looping road.

key: Speed Post vs ordinary post at India
name: ch09_speed_post_vs_ordinary_batch
alt: A customer sends a letter by speed post which leaves immediately, while ordinary letters wait until a whole bag is full before the van leaves.
scene: An Indian post office interior and its back loading yard, viewed in a wide cutaway. LEFT: at a counter marked with a lightning icon, a man in his 30s in office clothes pays a higher fee, a big coin icon above, and a clerk immediately hands his envelope to a motorbike courier in a khaki uniform who zooms out of the side gate with it, motion lines behind him. RIGHT: at the ordinary counter, a grandmother in a cotton saree pays a small coin and drops her letter into a large canvas mail bag hanging open on a stand; the bag is slowly filling with many letters. Outside in the yard, a red postal van waits with its back doors open and its driver sipping tea on the bumper, a clock showing he will not leave until the bag is full. A small inset at the far right shows the full bag being tied up and thrown into the van, which then leaves with dozens of letters at once. Warm afternoon light, dusty yard, unhurried mood on the right. Labels: "ONLINE" over the fast counter, "BATCH" over the filling mail bag.

key: Streaming is a cricket commentator
name: ch09_commentator_streaming
alt: A cricket commentator calls each ball live, a fan reads a scorecard after the match, and a newspaper prints horoscopes for all twelve signs the night before.
scene: A triptych of three tall panels separated by thin vertical lines. LEFT panel: inside a stadium commentary box overlooking a bright green cricket field, an excited commentator in his 40s with a headset and a blazer leans to the microphone, a stream of short speech bubbles flowing out ball by ball, each containing a small icon (a four, a dot, a wicket); fans at home in a small inset hear each one as it happens. MIDDLE panel: a fan in his 60s in a cardigan sits at home after the match with a printed scorecard, reading the full result at once with a cup of tea, a clock showing late evening. RIGHT panel: a small newspaper printing press at night, a printer in an ink-stained apron holding up a page with a neat grid of exactly twelve boxes, each with a simple zodiac symbol, ready for the morning; a stack of printed papers beside him, a moon in the window. Bright daylight in the stadium, cosy lamp light at home, inky night in the press. Labels: "STREAMING" at the top of the left panel, "NON-STREAMING" at the top of the middle panel, "PRECOMPUTED" at the top of the right panel.

key: passengers care how long their ride
name: ch09_local_train_latency_throughput
alt: A commuter on a local train checks his watch for his ride time, while a railway official on the platform counts people moved per hour and how full each train runs.
scene: A busy suburban railway platform in an Indian city at morning rush hour, a crowded local train pulling in with people hanging at the doors. FOREGROUND left: inside the train doorway, a commuter in his 30s in a white shirt and backpack checks his wristwatch, a stopwatch bubble above him showing his ride time. FOREGROUND right: on the platform, a railway official in a white uniform with a cap and a clipboard stands near a big electronic board; the board shows a simple tally of passengers per hour with a rising counter. Above the arriving train, each coach is drawn with a small fill gauge showing how full it is, some nearly full, one half empty. In the background, another train departs in the opposite direction, and a second official in an office window above the platform looks at a chart of trains per hour. Bright morning sunlight, steel and concrete, energetic crowds, a chai vendor with a kettle weaving through. Labels: "LATENCY" above the commuter's stopwatch, "THROUGHPUT" on the passenger tally board, "UTILIZATION" over the coach fill gauges.

key: TTFT is how long until the first plate
name: ch09_restaurant_ttft_tpot
alt: Diners wait for the first plate to land, then see later plates arrive at intervals, while the kitchen secretly phones a supplier before cooking.
scene: A cutaway view of an Indian restaurant, the dining room on the left and the kitchen on the right. LEFT: a family of four, parents in their 40s and two children, sits at a table with empty plates, the father checking his watch; a long dotted timeline runs along the table edge from the moment they ordered to the first plate of starters landing, marked with a stopwatch. After that, smaller evenly spaced dots mark the arrival of later plates, a second plate of rotis and a third plate of curry, each with a short gap. RIGHT: in the kitchen, before any cooking begins, the head cook in a white cap stands holding a wall phone to his ear, talking to a supplier, a speech bubble with a crate of vegetables; behind him the stoves are still cold, but a small icon shows the kitchen is busy. A curtain between the rooms hides this from the diners, who only see their empty table. Warm restaurant lighting on the left, brighter kitchen light on the right. Labels: "TTFT" along the long first wait, "TPOT" between the later plate dots, "HIDDEN WORK" over the phone call.

key: nine take ~30 minutes, one got stuck
name: ch09_commute_average_vs_median
alt: Nine friends arrive at the office in about thirty minutes, while one is stuck for hours behind a broken-down bus, making the average misleading.
scene: A wide composition of an Indian city morning. On the right, an office building entrance where nine friends in office clothes, a mix of men and women in shirts, kurtas and lanyards, arrive at about the same time, chatting, with small clock icons above them all showing roughly the same short time. On the left, far back down a long road, the tenth friend, a young man in a pink shirt, sits in a car stuck behind a broken-down city bus with its bonnet open and a mechanic under it, a long queue of honking vehicles, a big clock above him showing hours passing, and his face showing exhausted resignation. In the middle foreground, a whiteboard on an easel shows ten small figure icons, nine standing close together and one far off, with a tall arrow pointing at a spot between them labelled with a question mark where nobody actually stands, and a second arrow pointing at the middle of the cluster. Bright morning light, smoggy haze on the stuck road. Labels: "AVERAGE" beside the arrow pointing at the empty spot, "MEDIAN" beside the arrow into the cluster, "MAX" above the stuck friend.

key: paid per hour: the more rides per hour
name: ch09_cab_driver_pooling_throughput
alt: A cab driver paid by the hour picks up more riders by pooling, making each ride cheaper, though each passenger's trip takes a little longer.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same cab driver in both halves: a cheerful man in his 30s with a short beard and a checked shirt, a phone on a dashboard mount, driving a white hatchback through Indian city streets. LEFT panel: he carries one passenger, a young woman with a laptop bag, directly from pickup to drop, a straight short route on a small map inset; a small hour-glass and a single-coin icon show one ride per trip, and a rupee price tag on her side is high. RIGHT panel: he now carries three passengers who share the car, a student, an office worker and a grandmother with a shopping bag; the map inset shows a slightly longer winding route with three pickup and drop pins, and each passenger's price tag is smaller; one passenger glances at her watch slightly impatiently. A small counter above the right car shows more rides completed per hour. Bright midday street scene with buses and autos. Labels: "ONE RIDE" at the top of the left panel, "POOLED" at the top of the right panel, "THROUGHPUT" beside the rides-per-hour counter.

key: finishes 10 orders an hour but 7 arrive
name: ch09_delivery_goodput_cold_meals
alt: A delivery rider completes ten orders in an hour, but seven meals arrive cold, so only three count as good deliveries under the promise.
scene: A wide street view of an Indian city at lunchtime, laid out as a loop of ten doorsteps around a central restaurant. A delivery rider in his 20s in an orange jacket and helmet zips around on a scooter with an insulated box, his route drawn as a looping dotted line touching each doorstep. At each doorstep, a customer opens a food packet: at three doors, steam rises, the customers smile, and a small green tick floats above; at seven doors, the food has a little blue snowflake icon, the customers frown or shrug, and a grey cross floats above. At the centre, a big billboard-style banner from the delivery app shows a steaming plate and a clock icon promising hot food within thirty minutes. In the foreground, a manager in her 30s with a tablet counts on a tally board: ten marks in one row, only three marks in a second row highlighted in gold. Bright noon sun, busy traffic, autos and handcarts crowding the lanes. Labels: "SLO" on the promise banner, "THROUGHPUT" over the row of ten marks, "GOODPUT" over the row of three gold marks.

key: carries one passenger per trip
name: ch09_empty_bus_mfu
alt: A forty-seat bus runs all day but carries only one passenger per trip, so the depot logbook says fully used while almost every seat is empty.
scene: A long city bus in an Indian depot and on the road, shown in a cutaway side view so all forty seats are visible inside. Only one passenger sits in the whole bus, an old man in a dhoti and a white shirt holding an umbrella, in the third row; the other thirty-nine seats are drawn empty with faint seat outlines. The driver, a man in his 50s in a khaki uniform, drives cheerfully, and a sun-to-moon arc over the bus shows it running from early morning to night without stopping. In the foreground on the right, at the depot office desk, a clerk in his 40s with spectacles proudly holds up a logbook with a full row of green ticks for every hour of the day. Above the bus, a small seat gauge shows a nearly empty bar, a tiny sliver of fill. A depot manager in a cap stands beside the gauge, frowning and pointing at it. Bright daytime light on the road, a dusty depot with other buses parked behind and a mechanic washing one of them. Labels: "100% BUSY" on the logbook, "SEATS USED" beside the nearly empty gauge.

key: A water tanker supplying a housing
name: ch09_water_tanker_mbu
alt: A water tanker feeds a housing society; with one tap open the pipe limits flow, with hundreds of taps open the pump motor is the limit.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a water tanker truck parked outside an Indian apartment block, its thick hose connected to the society's pipe, and a pump motor on the ground between them. LEFT panel: early morning, only one tap is open on a ground-floor balcony where a woman in a nightie fills a bucket; water rushes through the pipe at full flow, a pipe gauge beside it reads near the top, and the pump motor hums lazily with little effort lines. RIGHT panel: evening rush, hundreds of taps open across every balcony of the building, residents filling buckets, a man washing a scooter, children with a hose; the pump motor now shakes and smokes, red-hot with strain lines, its own gauge pinned at maximum, while the pipe gauge has dropped to a middle level because the motor cannot push more. A society watchman in a blue uniform stands between the two halves scratching his head. Warm sunrise on the left, orange dusk light on the right. Labels: "PIPE LIMIT" at the top of the left panel, "PUMP LIMIT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Indian cricket before and after
name: ch09_floodlights_gpu_moment
alt: A cricket ground at dusk with players walking off for bad light, then the same ground under bright floodlights hosting a packed day-night match.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, showing the same cricket stadium in an Indian city. LEFT panel: a dim dusk scene, the sky turning dark blue, the umpires in white coats and caps raising their light meters while players in whites walk off the field in a line, a scoreboard showing play stopped; the stands are half empty, a few spectators packing up their tiffins and umbrellas. RIGHT panel: the same stadium at night, four huge floodlight towers blazing, a packed crowd waving flags, players in coloured jerseys with a white ball, fireworks bursting overhead and a big scoreboard glowing; a team of electricians in hard hats near the base of one tower gives a thumbs-up, and a cable leads from the tower to a big electrical cabinet drawn as a simple box of chips glowing. A thin arrow between the panels shows equipment arriving. Moody blue on the left, dazzling white and gold on the right. Labels: "BEFORE" at the top of the left panel, "AFTER" at the top of the right panel, "HARDWARE" on the electrical cabinet.

key: A CPU is a senior chartered accountant
name: ch09_cpu_accountant_gpu_clerks
alt: One senior accountant works through complex tasks one at a time, while a vast hall of clerks each does simple sums together in a flash.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a private wood-panelled cabin with a single desk, a senior chartered accountant in his 60s with silver hair, half-moon spectacles and a crisp bandhgala jacket concentrates deeply on one complex file at a time, a fountain pen in hand, a neat stack of finished files to one side and a queue of waiting files to the other; a single spotlight lamp glows. RIGHT panel: a vast hall seen from a high balcony, filled with hundreds of tiny identical desks in perfect rows, each with a young clerk in a white shirt and a simple calculator, all doing a small addition at the same time; a wave of little plus and multiply signs ripples across the hall; at the front, a delivery trolley piled with paper arrives through a narrow doorway, and some clerks at the back sit waiting with empty desks, hinting that feeding them papers fast is the real problem. Warm private glow on the left, bright fluorescent hall on the right. Labels: "CPU" at the top of the left panel, "GPU" at the top of the right panel, "FEEDING" over the paper trolley at the doorway.

key: scalar = rolling one roti at a time
name: ch09_roti_scalar_vector_tensor
alt: Three ways to make rotis: rolling one at a time with a rolling pin, flattening a row of four with a long roller, and stamping a whole tray with a press.
scene: A triptych of three tall panels separated by thin vertical lines, all in a bustling community kitchen at a gurudwara-style langar with steel counters, sacks of flour and huge tawas. LEFT panel: an elderly woman in a white dupatta sits on a low stool with a small wooden board and a rolling pin, rolling one roti at a time, steady and careful; a single roti sits finished beside her. MIDDLE panel: a young man in a turban and an apron pushes a long wide roller across a row of four dough balls on a long board, flattening all four at once, four neat rotis appearing in a line. RIGHT panel: a big cast-iron press with a lever, operated by a cheerful middle- aged cook with a moustache, comes down on a whole tray of dough balls arranged in a grid, stamping a complete grid of rotis in one go; beside it, one odd-shaped paratha lies untouched, not fitting the tray. Warm golden kitchen light, flour dust floating, steam from the tawas. Labels: "SCALAR" at the top of the left panel, "VECTOR" at the top of the middle panel, "TENSOR" at the top of the right panel.

key: goes twice as fast as counting each coin
name: ch09_counting_bundles_low_precision
alt: A bank cashier counts notes by the bundle much faster than her colleague who counts loose coins one by one.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves at a bank cashier's cabin in an Indian branch with a glass partition, a note-counting tray and a ledger. LEFT panel: a cashier in her 30s with a neat bun and a pale blue saree quickly moves banded bundles of ten-rupee notes from one side of the desk to the other, each bundle already wrapped with a paper band, a fast motion blur showing she counts by the bundle; a small stopwatch shows a short time. RIGHT panel: her colleague, a man in his 50s with thick spectacles and a sweater vest, counts a huge heap of loose coins one at a time on a felt tray, pushing each coin with a finger, small paise coins mixed in, his stopwatch showing a much longer time and his forehead sweating. In a small inset at the bottom of the left panel, one bundle has its band slightly torn and a missing note, with a small warning triangle, hinting that too much shortcutting can make totals go wrong. Calm bank interior light. Labels: "LOW PRECISION" at the top of the left panel, "HIGH PRECISION" at the top of the right panel.

key: An air-conditioner in a Chennai summer
name: ch09_gpu_rack_heaters_cooling
alt: A home air-conditioner strains on a hot summer day, beside a data-centre room where rows of glowing heaters are kept cool by huge chillers.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a middle-class living room in a hot coastal South Indian city at noon, the window showing blazing sun and palm trees; a window AC unit on the wall hums and drips, its fan blurred with effort, while the room is crowded with a family gathering, a TV, a fridge and a pressure cooker whistling in the kitchen; small heat-wave lines rise from each person and appliance, and the AC's power meter needle climbs. A grandmother fans herself with a newspaper. RIGHT panel: a long aisle of a data centre at night, tall black racks on either side, but each server tray is drawn as a glowing red electric heater coil, waves of heat rising toward the ceiling; huge silver chiller pipes and blue cold-air vents run overhead, and a technician in a fleece jacket with a tablet checks a big temperature display beside a warning light. A small inset shows a chip with a thermometer, sweating and slowing down when the cooling is turned off. Hot orange light on the left, cool blue and red light on the right. Labels: "HOME AC" at the top of the left panel, "COOLING LIMIT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Buying a vehicle for a dabbawala route
name: ch09_dabbawala_vs_highway_vehicle
alt: A tiffin carrier's route needs a vehicle with lots of carrying space, while a highway trip needs engine power; a sports car is wasted carrying tiffins.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a crowded city lane at late morning, a tiffin delivery man in a white cap and white kurta loads dozens of round steel lunch boxes onto a long wooden crate on a bicycle cart; next to him, a boxy tempo van with its back open shows racks holding hundreds of tiffins, and loaders quickly pass boxes in a chain. A gauge above them shows a full storage bar and a quick loading icon. In the middle of the lane, a sleek red sports car stands absurdly, its tiny boot open with just two tiffins inside, the driver in sunglasses looking embarrassed while the tiffin man laughs. RIGHT panel: a wide open expressway through dry hills at sunset, the same sleek sports car roaring ahead with speed lines, a big engine power gauge pinned high above it, a highway sign showing a long distance. Busy warm light and honking scooters on the left, golden sunset and an empty road on the right. Labels: "MEMORY" over the tempo van's racks, "COMPUTE" over the speeding car on the right.

key: The same biryani recipe at four
name: ch09_biryani_branches_optimized
alt: Four branches of a restaurant chain serve biryani under the same menu name, each with a small shortcut that makes it taste slightly different.
scene: A row of four restaurant shopfronts side by side along a city street, all with the same awning colour and the same menu board showing a steaming biryani handi icon with an identical dish name, so they look like branches of one chain. In front of each, a steel plate of biryani sits on a small table with a taster, the same food critic in her 40s with a notebook and spectacles, drawn four times. BRANCH 1: the original slow dum cooking in a sealed handi, the critic smiles. BRANCH 2: a cook pours cheaper, broken rice from a sack, the critic tilts her head. BRANCH 3: a timer on the wall shows a shorter dum time and the cook lifts the lid early, the critic raises an eyebrow. BRANCH 4: a pressure cooker replaces the handi, steam whistling, the critic frowns slightly. Small taste-meter dials above each plate drift a little from branch to branch, while the menu boards stay identical. Warm afternoon street light, delivery scooters parked outside. Labels: "SAME NAME" above the row of identical menu boards, "DIFFERENT TASTE" over the taste-meter dials.

key: it is heavy (size), it must stop at
name: ch09_local_train_three_slowdowns
alt: A heavy local train is slow for three reasons: its weight, stopping at every station in order, and the guard checking the whole platform at each stop.
scene: A long side view of a suburban electric train running along a raised track through an Indian city, its route drawn as a line of small station platforms in sequence beneath it. Three numbered callouts explain why it is slow. CALLOUT 1, at the front: the train's coaches are drawn heavy and bulky, with a big iron weight icon and the motor straining, sparks from the pantograph. CALLOUT 2, along the route: a row of station boards numbered one after another, the train stopping at each in order with a little red stop hand, no skipping allowed. CALLOUT 3, at the rear: in the last coach, the guard, a man in his 50s with a white uniform, a cap and a green flag, leans out of the door and looks back along the entire length of the platform behind him, a sweeping fan of sight lines covering every passenger, a small stopwatch ticking as he checks. Commuters crowd the doors and platforms. Bright afternoon sun, overhead wires, a busy city skyline behind. Labels: "SIZE" by callout 1, "AUTOREGRESSIVE" by callout 2, "ATTENTION" by callout 3.

key: Pruning is removing staff who never
name: ch09_restaurant_quantize_distill_prune
alt: Three ways to slim a restaurant: rounding prices on the menu board, a senior chef training a junior on the ten best-selling dishes, and removing idle staff.
scene: A triptych of three tall panels separated by thin vertical lines, all set in the same busy Indian restaurant. LEFT panel: a waiter on a step ladder rewrites the menu board with chalk, replacing long prices with paise by short rounded prices, the old long numbers drawn as faint scribbles being wiped away with a duster; a little compress icon shows shorter. MIDDLE panel: a senior chef in his 60s with a tall white hat and a big moustache stands beside a young junior cook at a counter where exactly ten dishes are lined up, each the house favourite, teaching him with a hand on his shoulder; behind them, a long list of rarely ordered dishes is greyed out on a wall. RIGHT panel: the manager, a woman in her 40s with a clipboard and a lanyard, peers at a lineup of staff, some busy, some idle; she gently taps one sleeping waiter on a stool, but the shelves of the kitchen behind wobble with small warning lines, showing it is hard to know who matters. Warm restaurant lighting. Labels: "QUANTIZE" at the top of the left panel, "DISTILL" at the top of the middle panel, "PRUNE" at the top of the right panel.

key: re-read the whole textbook before every
name: ch09_exam_reread_textbook_per_word
alt: A student writing a long exam answer must re-read an entire textbook before writing each word.
scene: An Indian examination hall with wooden desks, a ceiling fan and tall windows, viewed close to one desk. A student in his late teens in a white uniform shirt sits with one pen and a long answer sheet that has only a few words written so far. Beside him on the desk stands an enormous textbook, its pages flipping in a blur, and a circular loop arrow runs from the textbook into his eyes, then down to the pen tip, then back to the textbook again, with a tiny step counter on the loop. Each written word on the answer sheet has a tiny closed-book icon above it, showing one full re-read per word. His face shows calm writing but tired eyes from the reading. A small notebook tucked beside the sheet holds neat bullet notes of what he has already written, so he does not have to recall earlier words. An invigilator in her 50s with a saree and a bunch of keys walks past, glancing at the wall clock, whose hands race. Late afternoon light, dust in sunbeams. Labels: "WEIGHTS" on the giant textbook, "ONE TOKEN" next to the pen tip, "KV CACHE" on the notebook of earlier words.

key: the article assistant drafts the next
name: ch09_ca_assistant_speculative_draft
alt: A junior assistant drafts four lines of a tax return, and a senior partner reads all four at once, accepts three and rewrites the fourth.
scene: A chartered accountancy firm's office in an Indian city, wooden desks, box files, a wall calendar and a fan. LEFT: a young articled assistant in his early 20s with a bright shirt and an office lanyard types fast at a computer, producing a draft page of a tax return with four highlighted lines, a small speed icon above him. A dotted arrow carries the four-line draft to the right. RIGHT: the senior partner, a woman in her 50s with short grey hair, a crisp cotton saree and reading glasses, holds the page and reads all four lines at once in a single glance, a wide-eye scan icon above her. With a pen she places green ticks on lines one, two and three, and strikes through line four in red, rewriting it neatly in the margin. A small clock beside her shows a short time spent, compared with a faded inset of her writing every line herself with a long clock. A client file and a cup of filter coffee sit on her desk. Warm office light, efficient mood. Labels: "DRAFT MODEL" above the assistant, "TARGET MODEL" above the partner, "ACCEPTED" beside the three ticked lines.

key: Filling a railway reservation form from
name: ch09_form_copy_from_id_card
alt: A traveller copies her name and address from an ID card onto a reservation form and only thinks about the train number and date.
scene: A close, slightly overhead view of a writing ledge at an Indian railway reservation office, with a pen on a string, scattered forms and a glass partition with a clerk visible behind. A traveller in her 30s with a cotton kurta and a jhola bag fills a printed reservation form. To the left of the form lies her plastic ID card, drawn with a face square and grey bars so no detail is readable. Bright dotted arrows jump straight from the card's grey bars into the matching name and address boxes on the form, and those boxes fill in quickly with grey lines, a small lightning icon beside them. Only two boxes on the form remain empty, a train number box and a date box, and above her head a thought bubble shows a small timetable and a calendar, where she is actually thinking. In the background, a long queue and a big station clock. A small inset in the corner shows a blank essay sheet with no source card, the pen hovering uncertainly. Warm afternoon light through dusty windows. Labels: "COPY" beside the jumping arrows, "THINK" above the thought bubble.

key: pre-writing three possible lines for
name: ch09_commentators_medusa_heads
alt: A commentary team pre-writes possible lines for the next balls on cards, so the right line is ready the instant the ball is bowled.
scene: A cricket commentary box high above a floodlit stadium, a big window showing the green field below with a bowler running in. At the microphone sits the main commentator, a man in his 50s in a blazer and headset, ready to speak. Behind him, three assistant writers, a young woman with a ponytail, a man in a cap and an older man with spectacles, each hold up a small cue card with one ready line drawn as an icon: a boundary rope for a four, a dot for a dot ball, and falling stumps for a wicket; each writer is assigned to a different future ball, shown by little numbered tags pinned on their shirts for the next, the one after, and the one after that. Down on the field, as the ball reaches the batter, the matching card glows and the commentator grabs it instantly, while a small check icon confirms the cards fit together in sequence. A scoreboard and a cheering crowd fill the background. Bright floodlight glow, excited mood. Labels: "HEADS" above the three writers, "VERIFY" beside the commentator.

key: When a customer buys something new, he
name: ch09_kirana_khata_kv_cache
alt: A shopkeeper adds one new line to a running credit book instead of re-totalling every past purchase.
scene: A small neighbourhood kirana shop counter in the evening, with shelves of rice bags, oil tins and soap, a hanging string of chip packets and a brass bell. Behind the counter sits the owner, a portly man in his 50s with a white vest, a pencil behind his ear and reading glasses on his nose. Open in front of him is a thick cloth-bound credit book with many pages of past entries, neat columns of dates and amounts. A regular customer, a housewife in her 40s in a cotton nightie with a dupatta and a cloth bag, buys a packet of tea. The owner reads the running total at the bottom of the last page and writes just one new line below it, a small plus icon beside it. On the left, a faded inset shows the wrong way: the same owner frantically flipping back through every page since the start of the year with a calculator, sweating, piles of pages in the air. A tube light hums over the counter and a calendar with a festival picture hangs on the wall. Warm cosy light. Labels: "KHATA" on the credit book, "KV CACHE" below the counter, "ONE NEW LINE" beside the new entry.

key: MQA is eight students sharing one
name: ch09_students_sharing_textbooks_gqa
alt: Three study tables: every student with their own textbook, pairs sharing books, and eight students sharing one book, with bag space shrinking.
scene: A school library reading room in India with long wooden tables and ceiling fans, shown as three tables side by side from left to right, each with eight students in white and navy uniforms. LEFT table: every student has their own thick textbook, and under the table eight bulging school bags crowd the floor, a bag-space meter above reading full. MIDDLE table: students sit in groups of four or pairs around one shared textbook per group, leaning in together, fewer bags under the table, and the bag-space meter half full. RIGHT table: all eight students lean around a single textbook placed in the middle, one small bag under the table, and the meter nearly empty. Each student, in every table, has their own small notebook and their own thought bubble with a different doodle, showing each still thinks separately. In the far corner, a student reads only the last few pages of a book with a bookmark, drawn small as an inset. Soft daylight through tall windows. Labels: "MULTI-HEAD" above the left table, "GQA" above the middle table, "MQA" above the right table.

key: Making masala chai unfused: boil water
name: ch09_masala_chai_fused_kernel
alt: Making chai by putting the liquid back in the fridge after every step, compared with making it all in one pot on the stove.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a small Indian home kitchen with a two-burner stove, a steel fridge and a spice shelf. The same cook appears in both, a cheerful man in his 30s in a vest and checked lungi with a towel over his shoulder. LEFT panel: a frantic loop: he boils water in a pan, pours it into a jug, opens the fridge and puts the jug inside, takes it out again, adds tea leaves, puts it back in the fridge, takes it out, adds milk, and so on; numbered footprints and looping arrows between stove and fridge pile up, and he is sweaty and exhausted, a trip counter showing many trips. RIGHT panel: he stands calmly at the stove with a single saucepan, adding water, tea leaves, crushed ginger, cardamom, sugar and milk in one go, the chai bubbling up golden brown, and pours it into two glasses; the fridge stays closed. A small inset shows a tiny cup next to the pot, hinting the work is done in small batches. Warm morning light, steam rising. Labels: "UNFUSED" at the top of the left panel, "FUSED" at the top of the right panel.

key: A kernel is a tailor-made suit for one
name: ch09_tailor_kernel_compiler
alt: A master tailor takes a generic paper pattern and cuts it to fit one customer's measurements, swapping in his best ready-made pieces wherever they fit.
scene: A traditional tailoring shop in an Indian city with bolts of fabric stacked to the ceiling, mannequins in half-finished suits, a pedal sewing machine and a long cutting table. In the centre, a master tailor in his 60s with a measuring tape around his neck, round spectacles, and a pencil behind his ear spreads a generic brown paper pattern on the table. Standing on a small platform beside him, a customer, a tall slim man in his 30s, is being measured by an apprentice. The master's chalk lines adjust the generic pattern to fit the customer's exact measurements. On a rack behind him hang his best ready-made pieces, a pre-stitched collar, perfect sleeves, a lapel, and he plucks one off with a dotted arrow showing it slotting into place on the pattern where it fits. In a corner inset, a different customer with a very different body shape stands puzzled in a suit that doesn't fit, hinting that a new body needs new suits. Warm lamp light and sunlight from the shop door. Labels: "COMPILER" above the master tailor, "KERNELS" above the rack of ready pieces.

key: Upgrading a Maruti for a rally
name: ch09_rally_car_speedup_stack
alt: A small hatchback is upgraded for a rally in three stages: a tuned engine, a lighter body, and a navigator calling turns ahead.
scene: A three-stage left-to-right sequence at a rally workshop and track, set in a dusty Indian countryside with red soil, scrubland and a hill. STAGE 1: in a workshop with tools on a pegboard, a mechanic in grease-stained overalls plugs a laptop into the engine bay of a small white hatchback, a big jump arrow and a speed gauge leaping upward. STAGE 2: two workers remove the back seats and replace the bonnet with a lighter panel, a heap of removed parts on the floor and a weight icon getting smaller, the speed gauge rising a bit more. STAGE 3: on the rally track the car kicks up red dust around a bend, the driver in a helmet gripping the wheel, and beside him a navigator in a helmet reads from a pace-notes notebook, speech bubbles with arrows predicting the next few turns ahead, the speed gauge rising a final step. A rising stair-step graph runs along the bottom of the image joining the three gauges. Warm afternoon light, dust clouds. Labels: "COMPILE" over stage 1, "QUANTIZE" over stage 2, "SPECULATIVE" over stage 3.

key: Better: a prep kitchen and a line
name: ch09_prep_line_kitchen_disaggregation
alt: A single cook juggling bulk catering prep and plated dishes keeps diners waiting, compared with separate prep and line kitchens joined by a runner carrying trays.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: one overworked cook in a white cap in a small restaurant kitchen chops a huge mountain of onions for a catering order of fifty, while a ticket rail overflows with small plated-dish orders; through the service hatch, a row of diners waits with empty plates, one tapping a fork. RIGHT panel: a cutaway of two rooms joined by a corridor. In the left room, a prep kitchen with two cooks in aprons chopping vegetables, marinating paneer and filling steel trays in bulk. In the right room, a line kitchen with a cook at the stove plating dishes quickly and sending them out to happy diners. Along the corridor between them, a young runner in a T-shirt carries a stack of steel prep trays, walking quickly; a small clock icon above the corridor shows the trip takes some time. Steam, bright tube lights and gleaming stainless steel everywhere, busy and loud. Labels: "PREFILL" over the prep room, "DECODE" over the line kitchen, "KV TRAYS" above the runner.

key: A tiffin service that cooks the dal
name: ch09_tiffin_service_prefix_cache
alt: A tiffin kitchen cooks one big batch of dal and rice for everyone each morning and makes only each customer's special sabzi to order.
scene: A large tiffin service kitchen in an Indian city early in the morning, steel counters and windows with morning light. On the left, two enormous pots, one of yellow dal and one of white rice, bubble on industrial burners, stirred by a cook in her 40s in a cotton saree with sleeves rolled up; a big ladle serves the same dal and rice into a long row of open tiffin carriers on a conveyor-like table. On the right, at a smaller station, a young cook in a cap makes small individual pans of different sabzis: bhindi, aloo gobi, paneer, mushroom, each with a name tag on a clip. Every tiffin carrier on the table gets the same shared bottom compartments filled from the big pots, and one unique top compartment from the small station, shown by two colours of arrows. In the back corner, the big pots take up a lot of floor space, a small space-meter icon above them. Delivery men in white caps wait with bicycles at the door. Golden morning light, steam rising. Labels: "SHARED PREFIX" above the big pots, "UNIQUE SUFFIX" above the small sabzi station.

key: Packing luggage for a family trip into
name: ch09_luggage_cars_replica_parallelism
alt: A family packs suitcases into differently sized cars, and adds more cars to carry more relatives, while one giant trunk fits only one car.
scene: A wide residential driveway outside an Indian house on the morning of a family trip, with a marigold toran on the door. On the left, a father in his 40s in a polo shirt and a mother in a salwar suit try fitting luggage into a small hatchback: either three medium suitcases, or one giant steel trunk, shown as two small alternative thought bubbles above the car's open boot. In the middle, a whole extended family of grandparents, cousins and children with water bottles and snacks waits on the steps. On the right, three identical hatchbacks line up one behind another, each loaded with the same pattern of suitcases and carrying a different group of relatives, a grandmother waving from a window, children pressing faces to the glass; a counter above the line shows more passengers carried as more cars are added. A neighbour watches from a balcony holding a cup of tea. Bright morning sun, festive travel mood. Labels: "BIN PACKING" above the first car's thought bubbles, "REPLICAS" above the row of identical cars.

key: an assembly line making parathas
name: ch09_exam_split_and_paratha_line
alt: Four teachers each check a quarter of the same exam paper at once, and a paratha assembly line passes each paratha through four stations.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: in a staff room, one long exam paper is cut into four horizontal strips, and four teachers sit around a table, each checking one strip at the same time with red pens: a woman in a saree, a man in a sweater vest, a young teacher in a kurta, an older man with a beard. In the middle of the table, they staple their marks together into one total, with small speech bubbles between them showing they must talk to merge results. RIGHT panel: a dhaba kitchen with a straight line of four stations from left to right: one cook rolls dough, one stuffs it with potato filling, one cooks it on a tawa, one packs it in foil; several parathas are in progress at the same time at different stations, while at the start of the line, a small clock shows the last two stations standing idle, waiting for their first paratha, with folded arms. Warm tube light on the left, golden kitchen light and steam on the right. Labels: "TENSOR PARALLEL" at the top of the left panel, "PIPELINE PARALLEL" at the top of the right panel, "BUBBLE" above the idle stations.

key: Translating a 400-page novel. Context
name: ch09_novel_translators_context_parallel
alt: Two translators split a thick novel down the middle, while in another panel one translator drafts the whole book and the other edits it all.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a quiet publishing house office with bookshelves, a window with a neem tree outside and two facing desks. The same two translators appear in both: a woman in her 30s with short curly hair and a cardigan, and a man in his 40s with a beard and a khadi kurta. LEFT panel: a thick novel is split down its spine into two equal stacks of pages; each translator takes one stack and translates it at their own desk at the same time; a thin string with a small question bubble runs from a page in the second stack back to a page in the first stack, showing a reference across the split that makes them call out to each other. RIGHT panel: the woman translates the whole book into a rough draft, a long ribbon of pages flowing to the man, who sits with a red pen polishing every page of the full draft. Soft afternoon light, scholarly calm mood. Labels: "CONTEXT PARALLEL" at the top of the left panel, "SEQUENCE PARALLEL" at the top of the right panel.

key: On day one you have one cook and one
name: ch10_restaurant_grows_components
alt: A restaurant grows from one cook and one counter into a full operation with a pantry, food-safety checkers, a head waiter, a supplier desk, a warmer of ready plates and staff who order on their own.
scene: A wide cutaway illustration of a restaurant building, read left to right like a growth story. FAR LEFT: a tiny original stall with one cook in a vest and one counter, a single customer. Moving right, the building expands into connected rooms, each newly added: a pantry stocked with labelled jars and sacks; a food-safety checker in a white coat and hairnet standing at the front door and another at the kitchen pass, holding a checklist; a head waiter in a black vest at the centre reading order slips and pointing orders to a tandoor station, a Chinese wok station and a dessert station; a single supplier desk with one clerk on the phone and a funnel of vendor trucks behind; a heated glass warmer near the counter holding ready plates of the most common dishes; and at the far right, two staff members in aprons confidently placing orders with suppliers on a tablet by themselves. Throughout, the owner, a woman in her 40s in a smart kurta, walks among the diners, watching faces, with small smiley and frowny icons floating above tables. Warm restaurant light, busy and cheerful. Labels: "GUARDRAILS" over the safety checkers, "ROUTER" over the head waiter, "CACHE" over the warmer of ready plates.

key: Without a screen, he answers from
name: ch10_enquiry_clerk_live_screens
alt: A railway enquiry clerk answers vaguely from memory, then answers precisely after looking at a passenger database and a live running-status screen.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, at the same railway enquiry window with a steel grille, a printed timetable on the wall and a crowded concourse behind. The clerk in both halves is a man in his 50s with a grey moustache, a pale blue uniform shirt and spectacles; the passenger is a young woman in her late 20s with a trolley bag and a ticket in hand. LEFT panel: no screen on the desk; the clerk shrugs and answers with a vague speech bubble containing a train icon and a wavy question line, and the passenger looks unconvinced. RIGHT panel: two monitors now sit on his desk, one showing a database table with the passenger's ticket row highlighted, the other showing a live map of a train moving along a line with a delay clock; dotted arrows carry facts from both screens into his precise reply bubble, which contains a small clock showing a delay and a platform sign with a number. The passenger nods with relief. Busy station sounds suggested by a big clock and crowds. Labels: "MEMORY ONLY" at the top of the left panel, "CONTEXT" at the top of the right panel.

key: A sweet shop packing boxes for Diwali
name: ch10_sweet_box_output_guardrail
alt: A checker at a sweet shop counter opens each Diwali box, repacks wrong sweets, rejects a broken seal, and calls the owner for an angry customer.
