scene: A busy Indian sweet shop during Diwali, glass display cases full of colourful sweets, strings of lights and marigolds, a queue of festive customers. Behind the counter, packers fill gift boxes on a long table. At the front of the counter stands the checker, a young man in his 20s with a red cap and an apron, opening each box before it is handed over, shown in three small moments from left to right. ONE: a box with the wrong sweets inside; he hands it back to a packer with a curved retry arrow. TWO: a box with a torn tamper seal; he drops it firmly into a red bin with a shield icon. THREE: a customer in a silk kurta raising his voice and waving a long order list; the checker rings a small bell and the owner, a dignified woman in her 60s in a silk saree and gold bangles, steps out from the back office. To one side, two packers fill two boxes for the same order in parallel, and the checker hands over the better one while the other is set aside. Warm festive lighting, bustling mood. Labels: "OUTPUT GUARDRAIL" above the checker, "RETRY" by the curved arrow, "HUMAN" above the owner.

key: Live TV vs recorded TV. A recorded
name: ch10_broadcast_delay_streaming
alt: An editor censors a recorded show fully before it airs, while a live cricket broadcast runs a few seconds behind with a gap where something slips through.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves inside a television control room with banks of monitors and mixing desks. LEFT panel: an editor in her 30s with headphones and a cardigan sits at an editing desk, scrubbing slowly through a recorded show on a timeline, and confidently snips out a bad section with a large scissors icon before the show goes to a television set in a living room shown in a small inset at the top. RIGHT panel: a live cricket broadcast; a producer in his 40s with a headset and a lanyard watches the live feed from the stadium on one monitor, with a delay bar of a few seconds drawn as a short conveyor belt carrying frames from the stadium monitor to the on-air monitor. Small checkpoint gates sit at intervals along the conveyor; between two gates, a frame showing a speech bubble with a jagged scribble slips through unchecked and appears on the on-air monitor, while the producer's hand reaches for a button too late. Cool blue control-room light. Labels: "RECORDED" at the top of the left panel, "LIVE" at the top of the right panel, "BUFFER" on the conveyor belt.

key: A company travel desk. Employees never
name: ch10_travel_desk_model_gateway
alt: Employees send simple trip requests to a company travel desk, which holds all airline accounts, enforces policy, tracks spending and switches airlines when one site is down.
scene: An open-plan Indian corporate office on the left and a dedicated travel desk counter in the centre, with a row of airline booking windows on the right. LEFT: three employees, a young intern in a T-shirt, a manager in a blazer and an engineer in a hoodie, each hand a small note with just a city pair and a day; none of them holds any passwords, shown by empty hands and a crossed-out key icon. CENTRE: the travel desk, staffed by an efficient woman in her 40s with spectacles on a chain and a headset, has a locked drawer of airline account keys, a policy board showing a seat icon with an economy class tag pinned beside the intern's name, and a ledger with a bar chart of spend per team. RIGHT: two airline booking windows; one has a closed shutter and a small red cross, and a dotted arrow from the desk swerves away from it to the other window, which is open with a green tick. Bright office lighting, organised mood. Labels: "GATEWAY" above the travel desk, "POLICY" on the board, "FALLBACK" along the swerving arrow.

key: A school teacher who has heard
name: ch10_teacher_semantic_cache_trap
alt: A teacher gives the same answer to fifty differently worded washroom requests, then wrongly gives the same answer to a child asking to go home.
scene: A bright Indian primary school classroom with wooden benches, a blackboard with the alphabet, and a ceiling fan. A teacher in her 30s in a cotton saree with a chalk-dusted hand stands at the front with a hand raised, answering automatically. LEFT side of the classroom: a dozen children in blue uniforms raise hands one after another with many different speech bubbles, each drawn with a tiny toilet icon but different scribbles and extra marks, and a single stamp-like answer bubble from the teacher with a small clock showing five minutes is copied to each of them, linked by matching dotted lines; she looks relaxed and efficient. RIGHT side: a small girl with two plaits raises her hand with a speech bubble showing a tiny house icon and a school bag; the teacher's same stamped answer bubble with the five-minute clock flies toward her by mistake, and the girl looks puzzled and alarmed; a big red caution triangle appears between them. Morning sunlight through barred windows. Labels: "SIMILAR" over the many washroom requests, "NOT THE SAME" beside the girl's house bubble.

key: A read-only clerk can look up your bank
name: ch10_bank_clerk_read_vs_write
alt: A new bank clerk freely checks a balance on day one, while transferring money requires a supervisor's sign-off and a daily limit.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves at the same counter of an Indian bank branch with a glass partition, a token display and a potted plant. The clerk is the same new hire in both, a young man in his early 20s with a crisp shirt, a tie and an ID badge with a trainee tag. LEFT panel: an elderly customer in a white kurta and white cotton boat-shaped cap asks about his balance; the clerk looks at the screen, which shows a passbook-like page with an eye icon, and answers with a smile; a green open padlock floats beside him. RIGHT panel: a woman customer in a saree hands over a transfer slip; the clerk's screen shows an arrow moving coins from one account to another, but before he can press the button, a supervisor in her 50s with a lanyard and spectacles leans in and signs a form, and a small meter on the screen shows a capped daily limit bar. An amber padlock floats over this panel. Calm bank interior light, ceiling fans turning. Labels: "READ" at the top of the left panel, "WRITE" at the top of the right panel, "SIGN-OFF" beside the supervisor's signature.

key: MTTD: how long until someone notices
name: ch10_water_tank_mttd_mttr
alt: A housing society water tank runs dry; a float alarm alerts residents in minutes, a plumber fixes it, and a botched repair causes a new leak.
scene: A cutaway view of an Indian apartment block with a big blue plastic water tank on the rooftop, pipes running down the building to each floor. Shown as a sequence of numbered moments. ONE: the tank is empty; on the third floor, a man in a towel with soap on his face turns a dry tap in a bathroom, frustrated, a clock reading early morning. TWO: on the rooftop, a float alarm attached inside the tank rings loudly with sound waves, and a second small clock shows just two minutes after the tank emptied; the society secretary, a lady in her 60s in a nightie and shawl, rushes up the stairs with a phone. THREE: a plumber in his 40s with a toolbag fixes a valve on the roof, a stopwatch bubble showing how long the fix takes. FOUR: a little drip springs from a new joint he just fitted, with a small red warning icon. Arrows link the four moments in a loop. Early dawn light, crows on the parapet, and a row of empty buckets lined up outside each flat. Labels: "MTTD" beside the float alarm, "MTTR" beside the plumber, "CFR" beside the new leak.

key: Monitoring is a thermometer: it tells
name: ch10_thermometer_vs_full_records
alt: One doctor knows only that a patient has fever from a thermometer, while another has blood reports, history and scans recorded in advance and can name the illness.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a clinic consultation room in India, the same young patient in both: a man in his 20s lying on an examination bed with a damp cloth on his forehead, flushed with fever. LEFT panel: a doctor in his 40s with a white coat holds up a single thermometer showing a high red reading; above his head floats a thought bubble with just a big question mark; he scratches his chin, about to write orders for many tests. RIGHT panel: a doctor in her 40s in a white coat sits beside a desk spread with a folder of blood reports, a graph of the past few days' temperature readings, an X-ray-like scan on a lightbox and a page of history notes, all already collected with date stamps; dotted lines connect them to her confident thought bubble, which shows a mosquito icon; she writes a prescription with a nod. A wall chart of the human body hangs behind both. Clean clinic lighting. Labels: "MONITORING" at the top of the left panel, "OBSERVABILITY" at the top of the right panel.

key: she tracks what predicts losing
name: ch10_cricket_analyst_metrics
alt: A cricket team analyst tracks dot-ball percentage, dropped catches and death-over economy, split by bowler, venue and match phase.
scene: A team analyst's room in a cricket stadium, a big window overlooking a green field where players train. At a desk with two monitors sits the analyst, a sharp woman in her early 30s in a team polo shirt and a lanyard, a pen in her mouth and a tablet in hand. Her main monitor shows three large tiles, each with a simple icon: a dot ball icon with a percentage bar, a pair of hands with a ball slipping out, and a stopwatch over the last overs with an economy bar. Beneath the tiles, a grid of smaller split views slices the same numbers three ways, by bowler with small player silhouettes, by venue with tiny stadium icons, and by match phase with a timeline in three segments. On the wall behind her, a crowded corkboard of other unimportant stats, crossed out with a red marker. The head coach in a tracksuit leans over her shoulder, pointing at one bowler's slice, nodding. Late afternoon light through the window, focused mood. Labels: "METRICS" above the three tiles, "BREAKDOWN" above the sliced grid.

key: quietly changes the cook. The menu
name: ch10_same_menu_new_cook_drift
alt: A favourite restaurant keeps the same name and menu, but behind the kitchen door a new cook has replaced the old one and the biryani has changed.
scene: A cutaway view of a neighbourhood biryani restaurant with the dining room on the left and the kitchen on the right, joined by a swinging door. LEFT, the dining room: the same signboard and the same laminated menu card on each table as always, a framed photo on the wall of the old cook; a regular customer, a man in his 50s in a checked shirt with a napkin tucked in his collar, takes a bite of biryani and frowns slightly, a small thought bubble showing three earlier plates with declining smiley faces, the latest one neutral. RIGHT, the kitchen: the old cook, a stout man with a grey beard and a white cap, walks out of the back door carrying his bag, while a new young cook in a fresh apron stirs the big biryani handi, adding ingredients differently with a casual flourish. A small inset of the menu card shows the old and new versions with an equals sign between them, while two biryani plates beneath show a not-equal sign. Warm, slightly nostalgic restaurant light. Labels: "SAME API" over the menu card inset, "MODEL CHANGED" above the kitchen.

key: Components definition: the list of
name: ch10_wedding_planner_orchestration
alt: A wedding planner holds a vendor list and a timeline of events from haldi to reception, coordinating flowers and lighting at the same time.
scene: A large wedding venue in India being set up the day before, with a lawn, a stage and a mandap under construction. In the foreground, the wedding planner, a confident woman in her 40s in a silk kurta with a headset and a clipboard, stands at a central command table. On the table lies a vendor list with simple icons: a chef's hat, a flower garland and a music speaker. Behind her, a big board shows four events connected by arrows in order: a turmeric bowl, a hennaed hand, a pair of garlands and a dinner plate, with a small hand-off tick between each one. Around the venue, the vendors work: the decorator on a ladder finishing a floral arch, a caterer arranging chafing dishes, a DJ testing speakers. Two parallel arrows from the planner run at the same time to a team hanging marigold strings and a team rigging fairy lights, both working at once. Golden late afternoon light, buzz of activity. Labels: "COMPONENTS" over the vendor list, "CHAINING" over the event board, "PARALLEL" over the flower and lighting teams.

key: A new dosa stall that opens first in
name: ch10_first_dosa_stall_learning_moat
alt: The first dosa stall in a neighbourhood has learned what customers like, while a second stall that opens a year later starts from scratch.
scene: A street in an Indian neighbourhood shown across two moments. LEFT half, a year ago: a brand new dosa stall with a fresh painted board and a single tawa; the cook, a cheerful man in his 30s in a white vest and lungi, listens to customers, a college student and an office worker, whose speech bubbles show a small oil drop with a minus sign and a red chilli with a plus sign; he notes these on a small slate hanging on the stall, and a growing pile of slates stacks behind him over time. RIGHT half, today: the same stall now busy with a long happy queue, the cook confidently spreading a thin crisp dosa with very little oil and a bowl of fiery red chutney, his slate pile now tall and well worn. Across the street, a shiny brand-new second stall opens with balloons and a ribbon, its young owner in a smart apron looking around uncertainly at an empty slate, and only one customer. A dotted line of time connects the two halves. Bright morning light, steam from the tawas, lively street life. Labels: "FIRST MOVER" over the old stall, "MOAT" on the pile of slates, "NEW ENTRANT" over the second stall.

key: Dictating a letter to a typist.
name: ch10_typist_conversational_feedback
alt: A man dictates to a typist and gives four kinds of feedback: correcting a day, crossing out a line himself, walking out mid-sentence, and asking if the address is right.
scene: An old-style typing office in an Indian town, a big black typewriter on a wooden desk, carbon paper, a stack of letterheads and a ceiling fan. At the typewriter sits a typist in her 40s with spectacles, a cotton saree and a pencil in her bun. The boss, a man in his 50s with a moustache and a half-sleeve shirt, appears four times around her in a ring of small vignettes, numbered. ONE: he holds up a finger with a speech bubble showing a calendar with one day crossed out and another circled. TWO: he grabs the typed page and strikes through a line himself with a thick pen, a bold glowing outline around this one to show it is the strongest signal. THREE: he walks out of the door mid-sentence, a half-finished speech bubble trailing behind him and the typist's fingers frozen on the keys. FOUR: he leans in, squinting doubtfully at the envelope, with a speech bubble containing a house icon and a question mark. The typist's face changes in each, from attentive to surprised. Warm afternoon light through wooden shutters. Labels: "CORRECTION" by one, "USER EDIT" by two, "EARLY STOP" by three.

key: A call-centre supervisor walking the
name: ch10_call_centre_sentiment_tracking
alt: A call-centre supervisor walks between desks, hearing one caller calm down and end with thanks while another grows louder and needs escalation.
scene: A large call-centre floor in an Indian city, rows of cubicles with agents in headsets, computer screens and a big wall clock. A supervisor in her 30s in a blazer and a lanyard walks down the aisle holding a tablet, listening rather than reading. Above two cubicles, sound-level ribbons rise from the agents' headsets like little waveform graphs. ON THE LEFT: a young agent in his 20s with a calm smile, and his caller's waveform starts tall and jagged in red, then shrinks smoothly into a gentle green line ending with a small heart and a speech bubble with a folded-hands icon. ON THE RIGHT: a young agent in a ponytail looks stressed, and her caller's waveform starts small and keeps growing taller and more jagged in red, ending in a spiky peak with exclamation marks; the supervisor turns toward her, raising a hand to signal escalation, and a senior agent stands up to take over. In the far corner, a faint inset shows a crackling phone line icon with static, a reminder that loudness may not mean anger. Cool fluorescent light, busy hum. Labels: "SENTIMENT" above the two waveforms, "ESCALATE" beside the supervisor.

key: At a sari shop, a customer asking to
name: ch10_sari_shop_regeneration_signal
alt: In a sari shop, a customer asking to see one more sari is comparing, but when the shopkeeper keeps showing the same three designs she gets stuck and the cost of each showing piles up.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, inside a traditional Indian silk sari shop with white mattress seating, walls stacked with folded saris, and a salesman unfolding fabric in a sweeping arc. LEFT panel: a customer in her 40s, elegant in a cotton saree with a handbag, leans forward with interest as the salesman, a young man in a kurta, unfolds a fresh, different sari in a bright new colour; four different saris lie spread out beside her for comparison, and her expression is happy and engaged, a small comparing icon above her. RIGHT panel: the same customer, now tired and frowning, surrounded by a heap of saris that are clearly only three designs repeated again and again, the same green, the same red and the same blue patterns; her speech bubble says "one more" with a tally of many marks; beside her, a small meter drawn like a taxi fare meter ticks up with every showing, a rupee coin stack growing. Warm yellow shop lighting, rich colours. Labels: "COMPARING" at the top of the left panel, "STUCK" at the top of the right panel.

key: At the start he takes measurements
name: ch10_tailor_trial_fitting_feedback
alt: A tailor takes a few measurements at first and later, at a trial fitting, the customer pinches the exact spot on a sleeve that is too long.
scene: A small tailoring shop in an Indian market lane, with bolts of fabric, a mannequin, a pedal sewing machine and a long mirror. Two moments shown left to right. LEFT, first visit: the tailor, a friendly man in his 50s with a measuring tape around his neck, a pencil behind his ear and half-moon spectacles, quickly measures a customer's shoulders and chest with just a few tape lines, a small card with three numbers being jotted; a long 20-question form lies on the counter with a big red cross over it, unused. RIGHT, trial fitting: the customer, a young man in his late 20s, stands before the mirror in a half-stitched shirt; he raises his arm and pinches the exact spot on the sleeve where it is too long, a small circle highlighting the pinched fabric. The tailor marks that spot with chalk, and a thought bubble above him shows the customer's arm length being noted on the same small card for next time. A cup of tea steams on the counter. Warm afternoon light from the shop door. Labels: "CALIBRATE" above the first-visit moment, "PINPOINT" beside the pinched sleeve.

key: a good teacher writes both possible
name: ch10_ambiguous_question_ask_class
alt: A teacher writes two readings of an ambiguous exam question on the board and asks the class which one they meant, and in an inset a restaurant owner asks only one table in a hundred for feedback.
scene: A split composition with a large main scene and a smaller inset. MAIN: a bright Indian school classroom with rows of students in uniform at wooden benches. At the blackboard, a thoughtful teacher in his 40s with a sweater vest and spectacles has written an ambiguous question at the top and, beneath it, two possible readings as two simple sketches, labelled with a big chalk A and a big chalk B, connected to the question with forked arrows. He turns to the class with an open, inviting gesture; several students raise hands, some holding up an A card, some a B card. INSET in the bottom right corner, framed like a photo: a busy restaurant with many tables, the owner in a waistcoat stopping at only one table with a smiling couple to ask a question, while dozens of other tables eat undisturbed; a small one-in-a-hundred dot pattern floats above, one dot highlighted. Morning sunlight streams into the classroom over dusty benches, with warm evening light in the inset. Labels: "ASK" above the teacher, "SAMPLE" over the inset.

key: who hands you a sample: you either
name: ch10_paan_sample_implicit_feedback
alt: A paan seller hands out samples and learns from who accepts or walks away, while a shop next door gets few feedback slips from only the happiest or angriest customers.
scene: An evening market street in an Indian town with festive lights, split by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a paan stall with betel leaves stacked in a wet cloth, small steel boxes of fillings and a hanging lamp; the paan-wala, a jovial man in his 50s with a red-stained smile, a white kurta and a white cotton boat-shaped cap, holds out small samples to passers-by. One man in a shirt takes the sample and points to order a full paan, a green tick above him; a woman in a saree walks on past with a polite shake of the head, a grey dot above her. The paan-wala glances at a small chalk tally on his stall with ticks and dots. RIGHT panel: a neighbouring shop with a counter and a box of feedback slips with a pen on a string; the box has only two slips inside, one from a beaming customer with a big star and one from a furious man shaking his fist, while many other customers simply walk away ignoring it. Warm evening light, lanterns glowing, busy crowd. Labels: "IMPLICIT" at the top of the left panel, "EXPLICIT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Voting in an election by secret ballot
name: ch10_secret_ballot_vs_raised_hands
alt: Villagers vote privately behind a screen in one panel, and in a village meeting raise hands in public under each other's gaze in the other.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a polling booth set up in a village school, a cardboard voting compartment with a cloth curtain; inside, a farmer in his 50s in a dhoti and turban quietly presses a button on a voting machine, alone and calm, a shield icon above the curtain; outside, a queue of villagers waits patiently, unable to see. RIGHT panel: a village meeting under a big banyan tree, villagers seated on mats in a circle, an elder on a charpai at the centre. Hands go up for a proposal; one young man hesitates, glancing sideways at a stern landlord in a white kurta and gold watch who watches everyone, and then nervously raises his hand; dotted sight lines run from the landlord to several villagers. A woman in the back row whispers to her neighbour while raising her hand reluctantly. Bright afternoon village light, dust and chickens in the yard. Labels: "PRIVATE" at the top of the left panel, "PUBLIC" at the top of the right panel, "PRESSURE" along the landlord's sight lines.

key: almost every restaurant is 4.2
name: ch10_star_rating_biases
alt: A food app list where every restaurant is rated between 4.2 and 4.6, the first listing gets most orders, and a glossy long description wins over a short accurate one.
scene: A large smartphone screen drawn as the centre of the image, showing a food ordering app list, with three callouts around it. On the screen, five restaurant cards are listed, each with a dish photo and star ratings clustered tightly near the top with almost no difference between them. CALLOUT 1 on the left: a diner, a young woman in a T-shirt, hesitates with her finger over a three-star button, a guilty sweat drop and a small sad restaurant owner icon in her thought bubble, and then taps four stars instead. CALLOUT 2 at the top right: a big stream of order arrows pours into the very first card in the list, while lower cards get only a trickle, regardless of quality. CALLOUT 3 at the bottom right: two dish description cards side by side, one long and glossy with sparkle icons and many adjectives drawn as wavy lines, the other short and plain but accurate; a crowd of thumbs-up icons flocks to the glossy one. Bright clean app colours on a dark background. Labels: "LENIENCY" by callout 1, "POSITION" by callout 2, "LENGTH" by callout 3.

key: A TV news channel that sees outrage
name: ch10_news_channel_feedback_loop
alt: A news channel's outrage segments draw more views, it makes more outrage, attracting outrage-loving viewers, until years later the channel and its audience have changed.
scene: A circular loop composition around a television news studio. At the top of the circle, a TV studio with a desk and a shouting anchor in a sharp suit pointing angrily at the camera, with a red flashing banner of exclamation marks. Moving clockwise: on the right, a viewership chart on a monitor in a control room shoots up as a producer in her 30s with a headset grins and taps it. At the bottom, a growing crowd of viewers in living rooms stare at TVs with angry faces, fists raised, popcorn bowls spilling. On the left, a data dashboard drawn as a big gauge with a needle pointing to more outrage, feeding a thick arrow back up into the studio. A thin calendar strip along the outer edge of the loop shows years passing. In the centre of the loop, a small before-and-after inset: a calm older studio with a soft-spoken newsreader and a mixed, relaxed audience, versus the current loud studio and an angry audience; no one in the scene holds a steering wheel, and an empty editor's chair sits off to one side with a cobweb. Harsh studio lights and red glow. Labels: "FEEDBACK LOOP" across the centre, "NO EDITOR" above the empty chair.

key: Learning time is like a monthly mobile
name: ch11_learning_time_data_pack
alt: Two young engineers with the same monthly data pack: one spends it all on short videos and has none left for an important video call, the other saves enough.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a shared rented flat in an Indian city with a mattress on the floor, a laptop and posters. In each half, a big battery-like data gauge floats above the person, the same size at the start of the month. LEFT panel: a young man in his early 20s in shorts lies on a bean bag scrolling short videos on his phone late at night, a ribbon of tiny video tiles pouring out of the screen; his data gauge is drained to an empty red sliver. In a small inset, the next morning, he sits in a formal shirt for an important interview call, but the laptop shows a frozen video with a spinning wheel and he looks panicked. RIGHT panel: a young woman in her early 20s in a hoodie sits at a desk with a notebook and a course video paused, her data gauge still more than half full; in her inset, she confidently takes the same kind of interview video call, smiling, the connection clear. A wall calendar in each half marks the month. Night-time blue light on the left, warm desk-lamp glow on the right. Labels: "WASTED" at the top of the left panel, "INVESTED" at the top of the right panel.

key: UPI made payments systematic: one
name: ch11_upi_systematic_platform
alt: One standard payment rail sits at the base like a road, and many different shops, apps and services are quickly built on top of it.
scene: A wide illustrated cross-section, like a city built on a foundation. At the bottom, one broad, sturdy road runs the full width of the image, drawn as a glowing standard rail with identical QR code tiles set into it at regular intervals, and coins flowing smoothly along it in both directions. Built directly on top of this road, in a lively row, many different small establishments spring up quickly with scaffolding still visible on a few: a vegetable vendor's cart with a QR standee, a chai stall, an auto-rickshaw with a QR sticker on the back, a pharmacy, an online bill payment kiosk, and a school fee counter; customers of all ages, a grandmother, a student, an office worker, scan codes with their phones. To the right, a parallel second scene shows a similar road labelled for building AI apps, with five stepping stones in order along it marked by simple icons: a checklist, a speech bubble, a magnifier over a book, a wrench, and a server rack, and new app buildings appearing on top. Bright cheerful daylight. Labels: "ONE STANDARD" on the base road, "AI SYSTEM" over the second road.

key: The book is the lecture; the repo is
name: ch11_lecture_vs_class_group
alt: A professor finishes a lecture in a hall, and afterwards students keep receiving updates, notes and links on their phones from a class group.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a college lecture hall in India with tiered wooden benches and a large blackboard full of diagrams; a professor in her 50s with a cotton saree and silver-rimmed spectacles closes a thick book at the lectern as the bell rings, students in casual clothes packing their bags, a wall clock showing the end of the hour. RIGHT panel: later that evening, three of the same students in different places, one at a hostel desk with a lamp, one on a crowded bus holding a pole, one at a roadside chai stall, each looks at a phone; above their phones float the same stream of message bubbles with small icons, a new notes page, a link chain, a pinned announcement and an updated diagram, arriving one after another; a dotted line connects the professor's book in the left panel to this stream, showing that learning continues after the lecture. Warm lecture-hall light on the left, cosy evening light and city lights on the right. Labels: "BOOK" at the top of the left panel, "REPO" at the top of the right panel, "UPDATES" over the message stream.
